title: Complex differentiability detected by the underlying real derivative
statement: Use the usual fields $\mathbf R$ and $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $E,F$ be complex normed vector spaces, regarded also as real normed vector spaces by restriction of scalars. Let $f:E\to F$ and $x\in E$, and assume that $f$ is real Fréchet differentiable at $x$. Write $A=D_{\mathbf R}f(x):E\to F$ for its continuous real-linear derivative. Then $f$ is complex Fréchet differentiable at $x$ if and only if there exists a continuous complex-linear map $L:E\to F$ whose underlying real-linear map is $A$.
